classes.finest_note: Polling-station spreadsheets from the December 2002 vote onward on the RIK archive; 1990–1997 as total reports and scanned statistical publications.
classes.note: Direct two-round majority election for five years, at most two terms (Ustav чл. 114, 116). Until 2004 a round was void unless more than half the electorate voted, which voided the votes of 1997 (I), September–October 2002, December 2002, and 2003.
classes.locator: https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/extfile/sr/41934/Zakon%20o%20izboru%20predsednika%20Republike.pdf (чл. 1: Председник Републике бира се на пет година; чл. 21–23)

cadence.runoff_rule: A candidate needs a majority of those who voted; otherwise the top two meet again within 15 days (Zakon o izboru predsednika Republike чл. 21–23).
cadence.locator: https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/extfile/sr/31/Ustav%20RS%20cir.pdf (чл. 116: Мандат председника Републике траје пет година ... Нико не може више од два пута да буде биран)
cadence.vacancy_rule: The Speaker acts as president and an election is held within three months (Ustav чл. 120).

classes.name_en: Municipal, city, and Belgrade City Assembly elections
classes.finest_note: Since the 2022 law each local electoral commission must post its total report and per-polling-station results on the RIK site (Zakon o lokalnim izborima чл. 60); the RIK document register holds them unevenly from 2022, and the results application only Belgrade 2024. Earlier results sit with each local commission.
classes.note: List PR in one constituency per unit, four-year term, D'Hondt, 3% threshold (5% before 2020). Elections were held nationwide on one day until 2020; since 2022 units vote on several dates (3 April 2022, 17 December 2023, 2 June 2024, and later rounds). The 29 units in Kosovo and Metohija count in the official register but hold no Serbian local elections.
classes.locator: https://pik.skupstinavojvodine.gov.rs/docs/12026zakonOLokalnimIzborima_8a0a05bc-42ad-46f5-b0ae-491ce61e66a1.pdf (чл. 1: Одборници се бирају на четири године; чл. 5)

cadence.administered_by: the municipal or city electoral commission (општинска односно градска изборна комисија)
cadence.locator: https://www.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/SlGlasnikPortal/eli/rep/sgrs/skupstina/zakon/2007/129/3/reg (чл. 1: Одборници се бирају на четири године; чл. 7)

access.evidence: Local commissions' decisions, lists, and result reports for the local rounds of 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026, posted unevenly (83 result reports for 62 units in 2024).
access.license: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 RS (stated on the Commission's website)

access.evidence: One scanned polling-board minute per station: 410 stations in nine units in March 2026, 225 in five units in 2025.
access.license: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 RS (stated on the Commission's website)

access.evidence: Belgrade City Assembly totals, by city municipality, and by polling station for 2022, 2023, and 2024.

classes.name: Избори за одборнике скупштина градских општина
classes.finest_note: Belgrade's city municipalities by polling station in the City Electoral Commission's PDFs from 2022; RIK's document register has separate city-municipality rounds for 2023, 2024, and 2026.
classes.note: 25 of the 28 city municipalities (Belgrade's 17, Niš's 5, Sevojno, Kostolac, and Vranjska Banja) elect an assembly of 19 to 75 members by list PR for four years, usually with their city's assembly and on the same polling stations (Zakon o lokalnim izborima чл. 95а).
classes.locator: https://www.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/SlGlasnikPortal/eli/rep/sgrs/skupstina/zakon/2007/129/4/reg (чл. 6: Статутом града се образују градске општине)

access.evidence: Results by city municipality and polling station for 2022–2024.
Polling-board minutes for Sevojno's five stations, 2026.
access.license: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 RS (stated on the Commission's website)

classes.name: Непосредни избори председника општине и градоначелника
classes.note: The 2002 Law on Local Self-Government had the president of each municipality and the mayor of each city elected directly, in two rounds; first held at the local elections of September 2004. The 2007 law returned the choice to the assembly (чл. 43) from the next local elections.
classes.locator: https://www.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/SlGlasnikPortal/eli/rep/sgrs/skupstina/zakon/2007/129/2/reg (чл. 43: Председника општине бира скупштина општине; чл. 99 repeals the Закон о локалној самоуправи, бр. 9/02, 33/04, 135/04 и 62/06; чл. 101)
classes.disposition_reason: Results were published only by each local electoral commission in 2004–2007; no official online record was found, and the 2002 law's gazette text sits behind the legal portal's subscription.

classes.name: Покрајински и локални референдуми
classes.finest_note: Polling-board minutes on the RIK site for 2026 (Ada); otherwise results appear only in each unit's official gazette.
classes.note: Called by the provincial assembly or the unit's assembly and run by the provincial or local electoral commission (Zakon o referendumu i narodnoj inicijativi чл. 10, 19); results are published the way the calling decision was (чл. 41). No official list of held local referendums exists.
classes.locator: https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/extfile/sr/11469/Zakon%20referendum-2021.pdf (чл. 10: локални референдум расписује скупштина јединице локалне самоуправе; чл. 19; чл. 41)

access.evidence: 21 polling-board minutes of Ada's 2026 local referendum.
access.license: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 RS (stated on the Commission's website)

classes.name: Избори за савете месних заједница
classes.note: Outside Belgrade the councils are elected by direct secret ballot under each municipality's founding acts, called by the assembly's president; in Belgrade the city municipality's assembly chooses them on the proposal of a citizens' meeting (Zakon o glavnom gradu чл. 50а).
classes.locator: https://www.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/SlGlasnikPortal/eli/rep/sgrs/skupstina/zakon/2007/129/2/reg (чл. 74: Избори за савет месне заједнице спроводе се по правилима непосредног и тајног гласања ... у складу са актом о оснивању)
classes.disposition_reason: Each of about 4,000 local communities votes on its own date under municipal rules, and no authority publishes the results centrally.

classes.name: Локални избори у општинама на Косову и Метохији
classes.name_en: Serbian-run local elections in Kosovo municipalities
classes.note: Serbia held local elections in Kosovo Serb areas with its own local elections in 2008 and 2012, outside the administration set up under UN Security Council Resolution 1244.
classes.locator: https://publikacije.stat.gov.rs/G2025/Pdf/G20252058.pdf (табела 1.4: 29 units of Kosovo and Metohija, for which RZS publishes no data)
classes.disposition_reason: Kosovo's municipalities sit in the archive's Kosovo census, which leaves these Serbian-run votes out of scope; no Serbian authority publishes their results.

classes.name: Избори за чланове националних савета националних мањина
classes.finest_note: 2014 and 2018 by polling station and municipality (RIK archive spreadsheets); 2022 council totals only; 2026 council totals plus scanned polling-board minutes.
classes.note: Each council has 15 to 35 members for four years. It is elected directly by the voters on the minority's special roll, in Serbia as one constituency by list PR with D'Hondt and no threshold, when more than 40% of the minority's census population is on that roll; otherwise an electoral assembly chooses it. Direct elections are run by RIK; the Ministry calls them and runs electoral assemblies. Dates counted here are the direct elections; electoral assemblies (3 in 2014, 4 in 2018 and 2022, 2 in 2026) are indirect.

cadence.administered_by: Републичка изборна комисија (direct elections); the Ministry for human and minority rights calls them
cadence.locator: https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/extfile/sr/124/Zakon-Nacionalni-saveti-2018-preciscen-CIR.pdf (чл. 10: траје до истека четири године од конституисања; чл. 35: Изборе ... расписује министар)

access.evidence: Per council: report, results by polling station and by municipality (XLS), and seat decisions for 2014 and 2018.
access.license: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 RS (stated on the Commission's website)

access.evidence: Total-results report per council for 2022 and 2026; scanned polling-board minutes for 2026.
access.license: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 RS (stated on the Commission's website)

dates.note: First elections under the 2009 law, run by the Ministry; no official record of the date or results was reached.

dates.quote: Избори за чланове националних савета националних мањина, одржани 2014. године НА НЕПОСРЕДНИМ ИЗБОРИМА
dates.note: 17 councils elected directly; 3 (Macedonian, Montenegrin, Croatian) by electoral assembly.

dates.quote: Избори за чланове националних савета националних мањина 2018. године, 4. новембар 2018. године
dates.note: 18 councils elected directly; 4 by electoral assembly.

dates.quote: ИЗВЕШТАЈ О УКУПНИМ РЕЗУЛТАТИМА ИЗБОРА ЗА ЧЛАНОВЕ НАЦИОНАЛНОГ САВЕТА ... 13. новембра 2022
dates.note: 19 councils elected directly (one report each); 4 by electoral assembly.

dates.quote: Чланови националних савета 21 националне мањине бирају се на непосредним изборима
dates.note: Repeat voting ordered for 22 November 2026 at some stations.

classes.name: Избори за савезне посланике у Веће грађана и Веће република Савезне скупштине (у Србији)
classes.name_en: Federal Assembly of Yugoslavia elections (in Serbia)
classes.note: Direct elections to the Chamber of Citizens on 31 May 1992, 20 December 1992, 3 November 1996, and 24 September 2000 (138 seats across the federation), and to the Chamber of Republics on 24 September 2000 (40 seats). Serbia is the legal successor of the federation.
classes.locator: https://publikacije.stat.gov.rs/G2001/pdf/G20016001.pdf (IZBORNE LISTE PREMA DOBIJENIM MANDATIMA U SAVEZNOJ SKUPŠTINI SRJ ... 24. septembar 2000. godine)
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the defunct Federal Electoral Commission; no official online source gives results below the federation's totals, which survive only in the Federal Statistical Office's printed statistics.

classes.name: Избори за председника Савезне Републике Југославије
classes.note: The only direct election of the federal president, 24 September 2000; earlier federal presidents were chosen by the Federal Assembly.
classes.disposition_reason: Only federation-wide candidate totals survive online, in the Federal Statistical Office's 2001 pocket book; no official results by republic or municipality were found.

classes.name: Скупштина Србије и Црне Горе
classes.note: Its 126 members were delegated by the republics' assemblies in 2003; no direct election was ever held.
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect: delegated by the republican assemblies, with no popular vote.

classes.name: Избори за народне посланике Народне скупштине НР / СР Србије
classes.name_en: Assembly of the People's (Socialist) Republic of Serbia elections (1946–1969)
classes.note: Single-list elections: the Constituent Assembly on 10 November 1946 (287 deputies), then March 1951, November 1953, 1958, 1963, 1967, and 1969; voting by rubber ball until 1953.
classes.locator: https://www.parlament.gov.rs/народна-скупштина/историјат/после-другог-светског-рата.126.html (Први скупштински избори у Србији после Другог светског рата одржани су 10. новембра 1946. године)
classes.disposition_reason: No official source online gives the votes; they survive only in printed statistics of the period.

classes.name: Делегатски избори Скупштине СР Србије и скупштина општина
classes.note: From 1974 voters chose delegations at their work and local communities, which in turn sent delegates to the municipal and republic assemblies (terms from 1974, 1978, 1982, and 1986).
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect: no popular vote chose the assembly's members.

classes.name: Избори за народне одборе и скупштине општина (1945–1974)
classes.name_en: People's committee and municipal assembly elections (1945–1974)
classes.note: Local people's committees, then municipal assemblies, were chosen by direct single-list elections until the delegate system.
classes.disposition_reason: No official online record of the votes; only printed statistics of the period.

classes.name: Избори за народне посланике Народне скупштине Кнежевине и Краљевине Србије
classes.name_en: National Assembly elections of the Principality and Kingdom of Serbia (1858–1912)
classes.note: The first law on the assembly (28 October 1858) convened the St. Andrew's Assembly, elected one deputy per set number of tax heads; the first election law followed in 1870. Under the 1869 constitution the prince appointed one deputy for every three elected; from 1888 all deputies were elected, by list PR from 1903. Voting was public until 1888.
classes.locator: https://www.parlament.gov.rs/народна-скупштина/историјат/историјат-1804---1918.117.html (Први закон о народној скупштини Србије донет је 28. октобра 1858. године ... Исте године донет је и први закон о избору народних посланика)
classes.disposition_reason: The National Assembly's history gives no election dates or votes, and no official digital record of the results was found.

classes.name: Избори за савезну скупштину Краљевине СХС / Југославије и ФНРЈ / СФРЈ
classes.note: Elections to the parliaments of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (Yugoslavia) and of federal socialist Yugoslavia, held across all of today's successor states.
classes.disposition_reason: These belong to a Yugoslav polity shared by all the successor states, not to Serbia's census.

classes.name: Скупштина Аутономне покрајине Косово и Метохија
classes.name_en: Assembly of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija
classes.note: The provincial assembly was chosen through the delegate system until 1990; Serbia has held no election to it since, and after 1999 Kosovo was placed under UN administration.
classes.disposition_reason: No direct election to it has ever been held; Kosovo's own assemblies are in the archive's Kosovo census.

classes.name: Посредни избори (Влада, председник Скупштине, покрајинска влада, председници општина и градоначелници)
classes.name_en: Indirect elections (government, speakers, provincial government, mayors)
classes.note: The National Assembly elects the government and its speaker; the provincial assembly the provincial government; since 2008 each local assembly elects the president of the municipality or the mayor (Zakon o lokalnoj samoupravi чл. 43).
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect: chosen by assemblies, not by voters.

classes.name: Избори изборних чланова Високог савета судства и Високог савета тужилаштва
classes.note: Judges elect six members of the High Judicial Council (and prosecutors their members of the High Prosecutorial Council) in ballots run by the councils' own commissions.
classes.locator: https://vss.sud.rs/api/documents/preview/zakon_o_visokom_savetu_sudstva_08_04_2026_14_47_21.pdf (чл. 7: Чланови Савета су шест судија које бирају судије; чл. 28, 29)
classes.disposition_reason: Only judges or prosecutors vote; the public elects no judicial office in Serbia.

classes.name: Унутарстраначки избори кандидата
classes.note: Parties and citizens' groups compile their lists and nominate candidates under their own rules; the electoral laws require only voters' signatures.
classes.disposition_reason: No state-run nominating contest exists in Serbia.
